assessments.reasoning: Authenticity passes because the License page is published by the GCC project on gcc.gnu.org at the exact GCC 14.2.0 GNU libstdc++ manual locator. Integrity passes for the controlled inspection because the page renders the relevant passage intact, the GCC 14.2.0 release tag identifies full commit 04696df09633baf97cdbbdd6e9929b9d472161d3 and lists COPYING.RUNTIME in its tree, and the separate COPYING.RUNTIME file is pinned to that exact commit. The file and passage agree on the title, version 3.1, 31 March 2009, and the exception’s relationship to GPLv3 section 7 as an additional permission. The manual’s COPYING.RUNTIME reference matches the release-tree entry and the pinned file’s path. No claim-relevant mismatch was observed. [Versioned GCC manual](https://gcc.gnu.org/onlinedocs/gcc-14.2.0/libstdc%2B%2B/manual/manual/license.html) [GCC 14.2.0 release tag](https://gnu.googlesource.com/gcc/+/refs/tags/releases/gcc-14.2.0) [Pinned COPYING.RUNTIME](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gcc-mirror/gcc/04696df09633baf97cdbbdd6e9929b9d472161d3/COPYING.RUNTIME)

limitations: The controlled integrity result covers the versioned locator and rendered passage in the release lineage. Cryptographic integrity of the manual’s raw bytes remains unverified.
The claim-record SHA-256 is caller-supplied and remains unverified. The public record was inspected through the Web rendering.

Support is limited to documentary identity and edition in this manual passage. It establishes no grant, file-specific application, distribution conclusion, crosswalk, or archival source-byte identity.
The active value is a proposed registry lifecycle state. Registry approval or adoption remains unestablished.

The claim SHA-256 was supplied as the public revision identifier. The operator checked the record bytes. The execution directly inspected the rendered versioned manual and makes no source or claim byte-capture assertion.
reasoning: Relevance passes because the code-license section directly identifies the named exception, edition, date, GPLv3 section 7 relationship, and file reference. Interpretation passes because the passage presents the exception as a distinct additional permission under GPLv3 and the revision 1 record defines active as a proposed index lifecycle state. Applicability passes for the named passage in the GCC 14.2.0 manual. Contradiction passes because the release evidence agrees with the passage and the separate documentation-license section addresses a different subject. That section assigns GFDL 1.3 to the covered documentation and says documentation generated from source comments follows the original source-code license.
